scenarios.concept: Empirical baseline reflecting frozen M2 trend intelligence with zero future scenario shock. Serves as reference anchor and regression verification benchmark.
scenarios.narrative: Current labour market conditions persist according to empirical 2024-2026 data. AI tools exist in early deployment; no accelerated technological shift is assumed.

assumptions.rationale: Baseline enterprise generative AI adoption rate across Malaysia as observed in DOSM and TalentCorp 2024 data.
assumptions.source_basis: TalentCorp Impact Study 2024 & DOSM ICT Survey

assumptions.rationale: Autonomous multi-step agentic workflows remain in early experimental pilot phases in general industry.
assumptions.source_basis: ILO Working Paper 140 (2025) baseline task boundary analysis

assumptions.rationale: Baseline task substitution rate for routine cognitive tasks under standard software tools.
assumptions.source_basis: ILO WP140 benchmark exposure

assumptions.rationale: Initial productivity enhancement from basic generative assistance and search tools.
assumptions.source_basis: WEF Future of Jobs 2023-2025

assumptions.rationale: Concentrated primarily in ICT, professional services, and multinational enterprise segments.
assumptions.source_basis: MDEC Digital Economy Report 2024

assumptions.rationale: Standard pace of corporate learning and public vocational upskilling programs.
assumptions.source_basis: HRD Corp Training Participation Benchmarks

assumptions.rationale: National AI Roadmap 2021-2025 baseline execution and initial TVET alignments.
assumptions.source_basis: National AI Roadmap 2021-2025 & NIMP 2030 Initial Phases

assumptions.rationale: Standard corporate procurement, change management, and governance cycle times.
assumptions.source_basis: Industry Survey on Organisational Agility 2024

scenarios.concept: AI adoption expands steadily across knowledge sectors. Workers leverage AI as assistant, summariser, and task helper. Human accountability, domain expertise, and strategic judgment remain central. Augmentation dominates over complete substitution in skilled professions.
scenarios.narrative: Enterprises widely deploy copilot tools. Routine administrative subtasks are automated, but complex decision-making, stakeholder communication, and quality verification remain human-led.

assumptions.rationale: Majority of knowledge workers adopt AI assistant software within integrated enterprise suites (e.g., M365 Copilot, Google Workspace AI).
assumptions.source_basis: Gartner & IDC 2025 Enterprise AI Forecasts

assumptions.rationale: AI systems handle bounded multi-step routine actions with mandatory human approval checkpoints.
assumptions.source_basis: MIT Work of the Future Task Decomposition Study

assumptions.rationale: Routine drafting, data formatting, basic code generation, and clerical transcription become substantially automated.
assumptions.source_basis: ILO WP140 Task Transformation Analysis

assumptions.rationale: Workers experience significant leverage in research, drafting, synthesis, and creative ideation.
assumptions.source_basis: Stanford/MIT Generative AI Productivity Empirical Studies

assumptions.rationale: Diffuses across major urban services, banking, ICT, and education, with moderate SME penetration.
assumptions.source_basis: TalentCorp Impact Study SME Diffusion Projection

assumptions.rationale: Active corporate training initiatives, HRD Corp levy utilization for digital skills, and university curriculum updates.
assumptions.source_basis: HRD Corp National Training Index Targets

assumptions.rationale: Targeted government incentives, NIMP 2030 digital mission execution, and AI talent development subsidies.
assumptions.source_basis: NIMP 2030 Mission 1 & National AI Action Plan

assumptions.rationale: Enterprises systematically adapt operating procedures, job descriptions, and performance metrics around copilot tools.
assumptions.source_basis: McKinsey Global Institute Enterprise Transition Benchmarks

scenarios.concept: Agentic AI workflows accelerate rapidly. Autonomous systems execute complex, multi-step workflows, interact directly with software APIs and databases, generate and validate code, and handle structured administrative functions. Human roles pivot strongly toward system governance, verification, exception handling, and strategic stakeholder interaction.
scenarios.narrative: Technological breakthroughs enable reliable agentic tool orchestration. Structured clerical, junior analytic, and repetitive programming workflows face sharp substitution pressure; system design, ethical oversight, and strategic coordination see surging premium.

assumptions.rationale: Near-universal deployment of autonomous agents across digital processes and back-office pipelines.
assumptions.source_basis: Stanford AI Index 2025 Accelerated Trajectory

assumptions.rationale: Agents reliably execute end-to-end task chains including software debugging, report generation, and accounting reconciliation.
assumptions.source_basis: OpenAI / Anthropic Autonomous Agent Capability Forecasts

assumptions.rationale: High-volume cognitive routine tasks face near-total end-to-end substitution.
assumptions.source_basis: ILO WP140 High-Exposure Substitution Modeling

assumptions.rationale: Engineers and domain experts orchestrate fleets of agents, achieving 5x-10x throughput multipliers.
assumptions.source_basis: Frontier AI Economic Impact Benchmarks

assumptions.rationale: Cloud API ecosystems commodify agent tools, driving broad adoption across public and private sectors.
assumptions.source_basis: World Bank Digital Development Trajectories

assumptions.rationale: Institutional Training Absorption Lag: Technology adoption accelerates faster than education and TVET institutions can redesign curricula, accredit programs, and train trainers. Training systems face severe capacity constraints, curriculum redesign lead time (12-24 months), worker cognitive absorption lag, and employer implementation delays. Therefore, while absolute training spending remains elevated, the effective reskilling absorption relative to the velocity of agentic technological disruption is weaker (45.0) than under steady copilot evolution (60.0).
assumptions.source_basis: Cedefop Skills Foresight Friction Modeling & Tinbergen Race Model

assumptions.rationale: Regulatory & Statutory Adjustment Lag: Government prioritizes worker safety nets and AI governance, but formal statutory processes inevitably experience public consultation lag, legislative drafting cycles, cross-agency coordination friction, and enforcement lag. As a result, effective policy buffering relative to the shock velocity is slightly lower (60.0) than under predictable copilot evolution (65.0).
assumptions.source_basis: National AI Governance Framework & Transition Safety Net Guidelines

assumptions.rationale: Aggressive restructuring of enterprise workflows and rapid phase-out of manual handover pipelines.
assumptions.source_basis: Deloitte Tech Trends 2025 Autonomous Enterprise Analysis
